controls.label: Value matrix V (2×2)

resolved_previous_findings: A legal numeric 0/1 checkbox exposes scaled versus unscaled comparison.
All guided explorations can be performed with the fixed 2x2 editors and checkbox.
The earlier impossible suggestion to add a third feature column is removed.
Dot-product similarity explicitly depends on vector magnitudes and directions; it is not identified with cosine similarity.
Small matrix size is correctly stated not to prevent softmax saturation.
Equation transcription is explicitly labeled and editable matrices/unscaled comparison are separated from paper content.
limitations: Matrices remain 2x2; d_k=2 for every legal editor state. Actual-column computation is correct, but this showcase cannot demonstrate changing d_k.
Concentration statements concern unequal score rows. Equal-score rows remain uniform under either checkbox setting.
Row-wise weighted average means a convex combination of supplied value rows; values themselves need not be probabilities.
No training, learned projections, masking or full Transformer reproduction is claimed.

failures.name: independent_attention_teaching
failures.details: Preserve every control, computation, visualization, numerical case and equation expression. Correct teaching only: (1) why_it_matters and second explanation step universally claim sqrt(d_k) keeps dot-product magnitudes from growing with feature count. This is not guaranteed for arbitrary user vectors. Qualify motivation under comparable-coordinate statistical assumptions or simply describe the demonstrated fixed d_k=2 score-spread reduction; feature count is fixed here. (2) first explanation step describes large positive scores only by similar directions; dot products also depend on vector magnitudes and are not cosine similarity. (3) first exploration says weights [0.6698,0.3302] and [0.7311,0.2689] per row: these are first-row values, the second identity-query row is reversed. State the two rows accurately or identify the first row only. Keep source-supported claims within the supplied excerpt and label added assumptions as teaching background.
